text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Army chief General Jehangir Karamat denied charges the army was involved in rigging the February 3 general elections.
- Newly-elected Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said Pakistan is facing its worst economic situation and pledged to carry out major surgery and a drastic cut in expenditure.
- Talks between the Pakistan Muslim League and the Mohajir National Movement (MQM) are progressing and they will form a coalition government in Sindh, said Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif.

- Leader of the opposition in the National Assembly (lower house) Benazir Bhutto said she would consider accepting chairmanship of the Foreign Affairs Committee of the National Assembly, if offered by the government.
- Punjab province's share in the federal divisible pool will be 80.808 billion rupees in the next financial year showing a rise of 11.4 billion from 9.36 billion in 1996/97 (July-June).
- Pakistan has no plans to establish ties with Israel and will only sign the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty if India does, Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said.
- Indian Prime Minister has formally urged Pakistan to resume a stalled Indo-Pakistan dialogue at an appropriate level.

- The All Pakistan Textile Mills Association urged the government to immediately seek necessary changes and amendments in the World Trade Organisation laws which are discriminatory and contrary to the interest of developing countries.
- The government has borrowed 9.097 billion rupees from the money market through sale of short-term federal bonds at a high average cost of 16.96 percent per annum.
- Senior executives of leading commercial banks feel the new government may raise shortly at least $1 billion by creating the proposed fund for foreign debt retirement.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said his government would soon announce an incentive package for agriculture.
- The 1,292 megawatt Hub Power Plant has started functioning at full capacity, becoming the first private power plant to start full-fledged supply to the national grid system.
- Opposition leader Benazir Bhutto has supported Nawaz Sharif's scheme to mobilise funds from overseas Pakistanis for debt repayment.
